hiring_bar_summary.statement: Firm-published bar for the Summer 2027 Global Investment Banking cohort: expected graduation December 2027–June 2028 (bachelor's, or a master's completed within two years of the bachelor's), minimum cumulative GPA of 3.6 on a 4.0 scale, US work authorization (limited sponsorship noted only for STEM degrees heavily indexed in finance), English fluency, and strong analytical/accounting/finance/quantitative/modeling skills with intermediate Excel and PowerPoint (official posting, verified 2026-10-12). A finance/business/economics degree is explicitly not required, but solid numeracy is. The 3.6 is notably higher than the sophomore feeder's preferred 3.2 — the bar rises at the junior-summer step.

thesis_text: Bottom line: JPMorgan's Global Investment Banking summer program is the documented front door to its full-time analyst class — a nine-week junior-summer seat on an industry or product team, with full-time offers for the following year based on performance (official posting, verified 2026-10-12). Who gets in, per the firm's stated screen: students graduating December 2027–June 2028 with a minimum 3.6 cumulative GPA, US work authorization, and strong analytical, accounting, and modeling skills; a finance degree is explicitly not required, but numeracy is. What the firm says vs. what to plan for: the process is more mechanical than folklore suggests — application, then a HireVue video interview (invitation within 48 hours of advancing; complete it within 7 days or you are out), then banker interviews — and classes fill on a rolling basis, so application timing is itself a competitive variable. Routes in, ranked: (1) the junior-summer application filed as early in the cycle as possible; (2) the sophomore IB summer route where offered (documented for Latin America Advisory with a preferred 3.2 GPA), which builds the resume a year early; (3) the experience ladder underneath both — smaller-bank, search-fund, or corporate-finance internships plus networking, the reported-norm path for non-target candidates. Key dates: there is no single published deadline — postings close when classes fill, so verify on the live students site and treat 'early' as the deadline. Risks and alternatives: the 3.6 floor is a hard stated screen, a point higher than several peers' published minimums; candidates below it should weight firms with lower stated floors and referral-driven review. Offer to execute: build the application timeline and the networking list now, and rehearse HireVue-format answers before the window opens.
